scope: Synthetic provider host + executor + fake Cursor CLI process tree; not total OpenCode UI memory
baseline: Starting worktree snapshot at 84db6dc with pre-existing user edits

workload.description: Valid JSONL tool events with 4000-character irrelevant payloads, paced in batches of 128 with 35 ms pauses, then 300 ms hold and a tiny final response

method.metric: Sum of /proc/smaps_rollup Pss across each fresh host and its descendants, excluding external sampling driver
method.summary: Median of three per-run sampled peaks and median of three per-run time-weighted means
method.meanCalculation: Trapezoidal integral of sampled tree PSS divided by the interval between the first and last samples
method.reportedPrecision: Values rounded to two decimal places

limitations: Synthetic Linux workload, one concurrent job; not a real provider or live Herdr session
Mandatory provider consumption is exercised, but the real OpenCode UI/service is not launched
PSS measures these process trees, not whole-machine RAM or reclaimable filesystem page cache
Sampled peaks can miss short spikes; three repetitions do not establish universal savings
Native peak did not improve over optimized Bun; observed ranges overlap
Native execution trades process RAM for temporary disk storage and reduced per-event pane progress
